text.approach: Start at the Pioneer Gulch trailhead and follow the Pioneer Gulch Trail until it meets the Diamond Peak Trail. Leave the trail there and head straight uphill, trending toward climber's left, until you reach the southwest ridge. In winter, with the Summit Lake road shut, this is the easiest line to reach. In mid-May snow can still cover the forest road from about 4,900 ft, adding road miles on snowshoes, while the first mile of trail is often already bare.
text.overview: Easiest access when snow closes the Summit Lake road, and a handy way in for skiers after the bowls beneath the top. The trailhead at Pioneer Gulch gives a round trip of 7.5 miles and gains somewhat over 4000 feet. Hike until the trail joins the one named for Diamond Peak, then go directly uphill bearing climbers left to the southwest ridge. Stay on it until it merges with the south ridge, and continue to the top.

text.overview: A 7-pitch, 5.10- granite rock climb up Dome Peak's South Face, established as a new route around September 2, 2011 — a rarely-repeated alternative to the standard Dome Glacier route for parties seeking real rock climbing on the peak.
text.descent: The technical climbing ends just below the top, and a short scramble reaches the summit.
